Fun Fact. If it wasn't for the electronic starting system Lyle's loses this race.
Traditionally races where started with a starting pistol. The sound of the shot tells the sprinters to begin.
But sound moves relatively slowly, atleast compared to light which is how final times are measured.
So it takes 0.0035s for the sound wave to cross each lane.
Lyles & Kishane where 3 lanes apart, so Lyles would've heard the starting pistol 0.0105s after Kishane.
But Lyles only beat Kishane by 0.005s and so if this race had been started using the traditional method Lyles loses through no fault of his own. 
That's how ludicrously close this was, that the speed of sound itself could've made the difference.
Thankfully the Olympics switched to an electronic starting system in 2012, with an electronic pistol wired to 8 individual speakers behind each athlete.
It really goes to show how every little detail must be considered for events like this, even the slightest thing can end up biasing the race.
